strengths: The paper addresses a useful problem with an identifiable audience in code representation learning and program analysis: transferring information from source code and comments into representations usable when only low-level code is available.

The combination of an anchored source/comment encoder, a trainable IR encoder, and staged contrastive learning is a coherent approach. The equations, pipeline figures, and pseudocode communicate its broad structure.

The reported results provide promising empirical signals. Function-name accuracy improves from 29.41 to 33.41, and summarization BLEU-4 improves from 32.43 to 34.36 over the strongest corresponding reported baselines. Evaluation across four tasks, component ablations, and a CodeT5 extension provide useful breadth.

The manuscript supplies dataset statistics and several training settings, and announces public code, models, and datasets. The observed sensitivity to comment quality could be valuable to researchers building similar training corpora.
weaknesses: Necessary: Resolve the POJ-104 task definition. Sections 2.3 and 4.2 describe supervised classification into 104 classes, but Section 3.2 and Table 2 specify disjoint sets of 64/16/24 problem labels across training, development, and testing. Ordinary closed-set classification does not explain prediction of these unseen labels. If the experiment actually performs retrieval, specify its training objective, candidate pool, ranking procedure, and definitions of MAP/MAR/MAF1. This ambiguity affects a principal result and nearly all component analyses.

Necessary: Restrict the binary-analysis claims to the evaluated input setting or supply supporting experiments. The inputs are compiler-generated LLVM IR, rather than IR recovered from stripped executables. Figures 7–8 retain informative function names, globals, and types; explicit function-name stripping is described only for DIRE. Executables and compiler IR are not trivially interchangeable as the footnote asserts. Document compilation and symbol handling, and distinguish the demonstrated IR results from claims about practical stripped-binary analysis.

Necessary: Clarify evaluation independence and target construction. Section 3.2 says generation performance is evaluated on the validation set, whereas Section 4.3 describes test-set evaluation. Explain checkpoint selection and identify the untouched evaluation split. Also document the summarization references and comment-generation checkpoint, and explain how overlapping functions or repositories are handled across pretraining and downstream splits. The manuscript does not establish leakage, but it leaves these important validity checks unclear.

Necessary: Strengthen or narrow the component-level conclusions. PCL-only training receives 10 epochs, while the full model receives 30 or 70; interpolation also accompanies a change in objective. The assertion that PCL converged is not supported by convergence evidence. Controls should separate training duration, objective, and interpolation, or conclusions should concern the combined procedure. Likewise, the human-comment collapse does not isolate authorship from relevance, length, preprocessing, or optimization failure. Generated comments improve POJ MAF1 over comment removal by only 0.79 points, so the broader claims about substantial benefits and why human comments fail need controlled evidence or narrower wording.

Necessary: Distinguish textual reconstruction from semantic correctness. BLEU, GLEU, ROUGE, and exact match support reference-similarity claims, but do not establish reliable decompilation, preserved behavior, or long-range semantic understanding. No systematic human assessment is reported despite RQ2 mentioning human perception. Figure 8's positive example even displays an incomplete 'status << )' expression in both the reference and generated code. Correct the example and provide suitable correctness evidence, or limit the conclusions to the measured textual outcomes.

Necessary: Resolve implementation ambiguities that hinder reproduction. Equations 8 and 10 feed the sum of embeddings into the interpolation network, whereas Figure 3 shows concatenation. The prose and Algorithm 1 allow different modality pairings, while the displayed intermediate loss specifically contrasts a source/comment interpolation against binary code. Specify the implemented pairing policy, interpolation architecture, temperature, and whether gradients flow through the binary-dependent targets in Equation 5.

Necessary: Calibrate performance claims and correct numerical reporting. Single-seed results do not establish the repeated claims of significant or robust improvements. Reverse-engineering exact match increases only from 24.73 to 25.16 against GraphCodeBERT, while BLEU decreases from 71.56 to 71.14. Report appropriate uncertainty or temper these claims. Section 5.1 also incorrectly calls relative decreases of 2.07%, 7.46%, and 18.25% point decreases; Table 7 gives absolute decreases of 0.79, 2.85, and 6.97 points.

Optional: Condense the repeated human-learning analogies and clearly label them as motivation. A directly comparable IR or binary representation baseline would further help readers position the method.
